01

“and decreed therein its sustenance”

Two explanations transmitted from Sufyān al-Thawrī (Q 41:10).

854
Explanation from Sufyān No. 854: 1: 6

Sufyān al-Thawrī

English
Transmission wording
854: 1:6. Sufyan, on His words
"and decreed therein its sustenance": He said, the garments of Yemen are made only in Yemen, and the garments of Khurasan in Khurasan (verse 10).
العربية
854: 1: 6 سفيان فِي قَوْلِهِ وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَا أَقْوَاتَهَا قَالَ ثِيَابُ الْيَمَنِ لَا يَكُونُ إِلَّا بِالْيَمَنِ وَثِيَابُ الْخُرَاسَانِ بِخُرَاسَانَ (الآية 10) .
Edition record 371504 · p. 265Link to report ↗
855
Report from Sufyān No. 855: 2: 4

Sufyān al-Thawrī

English
Transmission wording
855: 2:4. Sufyan, on His words
"alike for those who ask": He said, whoever asks falls under this (verse 10).
العربية
855: 2: 4 سفيان في قوله سواء للسائلين مَنْ سَأَلَ فَهُوَ عَلَى هَذَا (الآية 910.

“And as for Thamud, We guided them”

Sufyān al-Thawrī

English

03

“Do you think God hears what we say?”

An explanation transmitted from Wahb ibn Rabia (Q 41:22).

857
Explanation from Wahb ibn Rabia No. 857: 4: 1

Wahb ibn Rabia

English
Transmission wording
857: 4:1. Sufyan, from al-Amash, from Umara ibn Umayr, from Wahb ibn Rabia, who said:
Ibn Masud said: I was staying beside the covering of the Kaba when three men came, a Thaqafi and two in-laws of his from Quraysh, with much fat in their bellies and little understanding in their hearts. They talked among themselves, and one of them said, "Do you think God hears what we say?" One of them said, ⦗p. 266⦘ "He hears if we raise [our voices] and does not hear if we lower them." The other said, "If He hears some of it, He hears all of it." I went to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and told him, and there was revealed: "And you were not hiding yourselves lest your hearing, your sight, and your skins testify against you," to the end of the verse (verse 22).
العربية
857: 4: 1 سفيان عَنِ الْأَعْمَشِ عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ رَبِيعَةَ قال قال بن مَسْعُودٍ إِنِّي لَمُسْتَقِرٌّ بِأَسْتَارِ الْكَعْبَةِ إذا جاء ثلثة نَفَرٍ ثَقَفِيٌّ وَخَتَنَاهُ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ كَثِيرَةٌ شَحْمُ بُطُونِهِمْ قَلِيلَةٌ فِقْهُ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَتَحَدَّثُوا بَيْنَهُمْ بِحَدِيثٍ فَقَالَ أَحَدُهُمْ أَتَرَوْنَ اللَّهَ يَسْمَعُ مَا نَقُولُ فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ ⦗p. 266⦘ يَسْمَعُ إِذَا رَفَعْنَا وَلَا يَسْمَعُ إِذَا خَفَضْنَا فَقَالَ الْآخَرُ إِنْ كَانَ يَسْمَعُ بَعْضَهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَسْمَعُ أَجْمَعَ فَأَتَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ فَنَزَلَتْ وَمَا كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَتِرُونَ أَنْ يَشْهَدَ عَلَيْكُمْ سمعكم ولا أبصاركم الى آخر الآية. (الآية 22) .

04

“Our Lord, show us those who misled us from among the jinn and men”

An explanation transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (Q 41:29).

858
Explanation from ʿAlī No. 858: 5: 8

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib

English
Transmission wording
858: 5:8. Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Habba al-Urani, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, on His words
"Our Lord, show us those who misled us from among the jinn and men": He said, Iblis and the son of Adam who killed his brother (verse 29).
العربية
858: 5: 8 سفيان عن أبي اسحق عَنْ حَبَّةَ الْعُرَنِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ فِي قَوْلِهِ رَبَّنَا أَرِنَا الَّذَيْنِ أَضَلانَا مِنَ الجن والانس قال ابليس الا بالسة وَابْنُ آدَمَ الَّذِي قَتَلَ أَخَاهُ (الآية 29) .
Edition record 371505 · p. 266Link to report ↗
05

“Indeed, those who say, 'Our Lord is God,' and then remain…”

Two explanations transmitted from Said ibn Nimran al-Bajali and Zayd ibn Aslam (Q 41:30).

859
Explanation from Said ibn Nimran al-Bajali No. 859: 6: 7

Said ibn Nimran al-Bajali

English
Transmission wording
859: 6:7. Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sad, from Said ibn Nimran al-Bajali, who said:
I recited this verse to Abu Bakr: "Indeed, those who say, 'Our Lord is God,' and then remain upright": He said, they are those who did not associate anything with God (verse 30).
العربية
859: 6: 7 سفيان عن أبي اسحق عَنْ عَامِرِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ نِمَرانَ الْبَجَلِيِّ قَالَ قرأت هده الْآيَةَ عَلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ استقاموا قَالَ هُمُ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُشْرِكُوا بالله شيئا (الآية 30) .
Edition record 371505 · p. 266Link to report ↗
860
Explanation from Zayd ibn Aslam No. 860: 7: 3

Zayd ibn Aslam

English
Transmission wording
860: 7:3. Sufyan, from Zayd ibn Aslam, on His words
"do not fear and do not grieve": He said, do not fear what lies ahead of you and do not grieve over what you leave behind of your estates (verse 30).
العربية
860: 7: 3 سفيان عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ فِي قَوْلِهِ أَلَّا تَخَافُوا وَلا تَحْزَنُوا قَالَ لَا تَخَافُوا أَمَامَكُمْ وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا عَلَى مَا خَلْفَكُمْ مِنْ ضيعاتكم (الآية 30) .
Edition record 371506 · p. 267Link to report ↗

Abū Ṣāliḥ

08

“Had We made it a foreign-language Qur'an, they would have said…”

An explanation transmitted from Said and Mujahid (Q 41:44).

863
Explanation from Said and Mujahid No. 863: 10: 2

Said and Mujahid

English
Transmission wording
863: 10:2. Sufyan related to us, from Said and Mujahid, on His words
"Had We made it a foreign-language Qur'an, they would have said, 'Why are its verses not made clear? Foreign, and [the messenger] Arab?'": [He said,] it is in the form of a question: this is an Arabic tongue, so how can it be foreign while he is Arab? (verse 44).
العربية
863: 10: 2 حدثنا سفيان عَنْ سَعِيدٍ وَمُجَاهِدٍ فِي قَوْلِهِ ولو جعلناه قرآنا آعجميا بعد لقالوا لولا فصلت آياته آعجمي عَلَى وَجْهِ الاسْتِفْهَامِ وَهَذَا لِسَانٌ عربي كيف يكون هذا عجمي وهذا عربي (الآية 44) .
